speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To understand the full picture, have you experienced any unintentional weight loss, night sweats, or changes in bowel habits recently? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, CEA, CA-125, and CA-19-9.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 8,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 12.8 g/dL, Platelets 275,000 /μL; Comprehensive Metabolic Panel: NORMAL READINGS; CEA: NORMAL READINGS; CA-125: Normal; CA-19-9: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal tumor markers and lack of systemic symptoms like weight loss, have you noticed any pelvic pressure, urinary frequency, or leg swelling recently? REQUEST TEST: Serum Albumin, LDH, and D-dimer. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Pelvic_CT, Chest_CT.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum Albumin: 3.2 g/dL; LDH: 145 U/L; D-dimer: 250 ng/mL. Abdominal_Pelvic_CT: Large right ovarian mass with associated ascites; no distant metastases seen. Chest_CT: Right-sided pleural effusion with compressive atelectasis of the right lower lobe; no pulmonary embolism or lung masses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results. The CT shows a large ovarian mass with ascites and a right-sided pleural effusion causing lung compression, despite normal tumor markers. Have you noticed any recent bloating, early satiety, or changes in your menstrual cycle? REQUEST IMAGES: Please review the specific characteristics of the ovarian mass on the Abdominal_Pelvic_CT for morphology.

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your age, nulliparity, and the presence of a large ovarian mass with ascites and pleural effusion despite normal tumor markers, do you or your family have a history of breast, ovarian, or colon cancer? REQUEST TEST: BRCA1 and BRCA2 genetic testing.

speaker: Doctor
text: While waiting for the genetic results, have you noticed any fluid leaking from your nipples or any breast lumps? REQUEST TEST: Mammogram and Breast Ultrasound. Also, please describe the texture of the ovarian mass on the CT scan—is it solid, cystic, or mixed?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Mammogram: Normal; Breast Ultrasound: Normal; Abdominal_Pelvic_CT Ovarian Mass: Mixed solid and cystic components.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Krukenberg Tumor (Bilateral metastatic ovarian carcinoma, likely of gastric origin, presenting as a large mixed solid-cystic mass with malignant ascites and malignant pleural effusion).
